title: ALMA survey of circumstellar discs in the young stellar cluster IC 348
question: How do the mm-continuum disk masses of Class II sources in IC 348 compare with those in younger and older regions, accounting for stellar mass?

what.value: Target sample and Spitzer IRAC SED-slope classifications

evidence.quote: Our sample was selected specifically from the work of (cite: Lada2006), whose sample was based on (cite: Luhman2003), and from (cite: Muench2007)

what.value: Comparison disk samples for Taurus, Lupus, Cha I, sigma Ori, Upper Sco

evidence.quote: Upper limit inputs for the "comparison" samples are as reported in the literature
We derived the stellar properties based on the spectral types taken from (cite: Luhman2003) and (cite: Muench2007)

recipe.method: Peak flux and rms with imstat; uvmodelfit point source (non-detections) or elliptical Gaussian (detections); detection S/N>4
key_parameters: Peak from 4" radius circle, rms from 4-7" annulus

assumptions: d=310 pc, T_dust=20 K, kappa=2.3 cm2/g at 1.33 mm, gas-to-dust 100

recipe.method: Stack 96 non-detections centered on stellar positions
10^6 Monte Carlo draws by spectral-type bin, CDFs, censored Peto-Prentice tests; comparison samples scaled to 310 pc and 1.3 mm with F∝λ^-2.5
assumptions: Spectral type as proxy for stellar mass

recipe.method: Bayesian linear regression handling upper limits (Kelly 2007)
12CO/13CO ratio parabola optical-depth correction; integrate blue/red channels above 4σ outside 3" mask
assumptions: Temperatures 20 and 50 K; no inclination correction

evidence.quote: we detect 40 out of the 136 IC 348 targets at $>$ 4$~\sigma$ significance
we find a clear signal of 0.14 $\pm$ 0.02 mJy
the average dust mass of the disks that were not individually detected is only $\sim$0.40 M$_{\oplus}$
The fitted linear regression for IC 348 provides a large intrinsic scatter of $\delta =$ 0.81 $\pm$ 0.15.
we estimated a kinematic age of 1800 yr
medians of $p_{\phi}=$ 2.3 x 10$^{-12}$ and 5.5 x 10$^{-9}$ for Taurus and Upper Sco
